scope: Restore autonomous CPU teammates in fixed-player matches; maximum native difficulty, original CPU foot selection, safe preference for requested passes; keep approved human controls/camera and native team tactics.
platform: Linux rendered software OpenGL with real SDL virtual Xbox input
windows_validation: Windows x64 crosscompiled and PE/DLL/media/ZIP checked. Windows GUI and physical Xbox controller were not run here.
root_cause: Native ElizaController disables on-ball decisions for every player on a team with human gamers, assuming possession will switch human control onto the carrier. Fixed-player mode must allow autonomous CPU decisions on that team.
changes: Enable original carry/pass/shot decisions on both teams in fixed-player mode.
Restore native CPU foot ranking; preserve human right-foot preference.
Set native difficulty to 1.0; keep formation, dynamic roles, man marking, supporting movement and attacking runs.
Allow native CPU goal-kick variation and sliding challenges on the human team.
Pass calls evaluate native interception risk/type and offside before getting priority; unsafe calls do not suspend normal play.
Do not let the human switch button alter possession assignments in fixed-player mode.

fixture_notes: The movement check waits for SDL acknowledgement and allows native reception time before measuring travel.
A pass call may expire when the CPU loses possession or has no viable lane. Match tests accept normal autonomous continuation instead of forcing a pass.
An initial AI test mislabeled enum 7 as a shot (it is a header); corrected to enum 8 and reran both complete fixtures. No gameplay code changed for this test correction.

The second fixture never entered the native central shooting zone (0 samples), so shot coverage comes from the first fixture. Both saved fixture logs were reevaluated with --validate-existing after correcting that expectation, retaining their original executable SHA and successful exit evidence.

The supplementary solo chest suites missed a running chest reception; full observations for both the current and previous binaries are recorded separately instead of claiming all animation regressions passed.
Finite fixtures check observed behavior; they do not establish flawless decisions in every match.
